overview:
The last 90 days show an enterprise AI agent market that is simultaneously consolidating and commoditizing. Salesforce is throwing enormous capital and product surface area at Agentforce ($1B ARR claimed, $1B Swiss investment, F1 partnership, WEM, Commerce GA) while its own analyst base (KeyBanc, multiple downgrades) openly questions whether any of it is landing with real customers — a credibility gap Decagon's sales team should be actively exploiting in competitive deals. Meanwhile pure-play competitors are moving fast: Sierra bought TakeOff to get long-horizon agent orchestration, signed an exclusive SoftBank distribution deal that took a Japanese client from 83% to 97% resolution, and is running at ~$200M ARR / $15.8B valuation — this is the most credible head-to-head competitor right now, not Salesforce. Intercom's $3B acquisition of Fin and the broader wave of 'buying data for AI' M&A signals that horizontal platforms see AI-native support as the acquisition target of choice, not a build-it-yourself problem.

Underneath all of this, the model layer is being commoditized at startling speed. DeepSeek, Kimi K3, GLM-5.2, Moonshot, and Mistral's Leanstral are collapsing frontier-adjacent capability to a fraction of the cost, while OpenAI and Anthropic respond not by competing on price but by pushing directly into agent orchestration and workflow territory (ChatGPT Work, GPT-Live, Claude Cowork, Claude Tag) — territory that used to be Decagon's differentiated ground. Voice is emerging as a distinct, well-capitalized sub-battle (ElevenLabs doubling to $22B, IBM and TELUS partnerships) separate from the chat/orchestration fight. The net effect: model access is ceasing to be a moat for anyone, and the competitive question is shifting to deployment reliability, outcome-based pricing, and vertical distribution — exactly the areas where the market narrative (Anthropic/VentureBeat: 'most deployments are glorified chatbots') suggests almost nobody has actually won yet.

themes.description: OpenAI (ChatGPT Work, GPT-Live) and Anthropic (Claude Cowork, Claude Tag, Teams integration) are no longer content shipping raw models — they're building persistent, autonomous, workflow-embedded agents that directly overlap customer-support and enterprise-ops use cases Decagon targets. This is the most structurally important competitive shift in the period.

themes.name: Voice AI as a distinct, fast-scaling battleground
themes.description: Voice is decoupling from general chat/agent platforms into its own arms race — ElevenLabs doubled to a $22B valuation and struck enterprise partnerships with IBM and TELUS Digital, while latency and self-hosted alternatives (Asterisk/FreePBX AVA) proliferate. Sierra's SoftBank Japan deal also underscores voice/contact-center as the highest-value deployment surface.

themes.name: Outcome-based pricing displacing seat/token pricing
themes.description: Both Salesforce (Agentforce Help Agent pay-for-resolution) and Sierra (Horizon agents, outcomes-based pricing) are independently moving to charge for resolved outcomes rather than seats or tokens, signaling this is becoming the expected commercial model for enterprise buyers evaluating support agents.

convergence: The market is converging on a single fight from multiple directions at once: frontier labs (OpenAI, Anthropic) are moving down-stack from raw models into persistent agent orchestration and workflow automation; CRM incumbents (Salesforce) are bolting agent products onto existing suites but struggling to prove real-world resolution quality; horizontal engagement platforms (Intercom) are buying vertical AI-native support capability outright; specialist pure-plays (Sierra) are racing to out-execute both by acquiring long-horizon agent tech and locking up exclusive regional distribution (SoftBank/Japan); and voice specialists (ElevenLabs, Parloa) are partnering into enterprise contact centers rather than building full agent platforms themselves. Underneath all of it, the open-source model collapse (DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM, Mistral) is stripping away model access as a differentiator for everyone, which means the actual points of collision — where Decagon will meet Salesforce, Sierra, Intercom/Fin, and OpenAI/Anthropic head-on in the same RFPs — are deployment reliability, outcome-based pricing, and voice latency, not model IP.

predictions.claim: Outcome-based / pay-per-resolution pricing becomes a standard RFP requirement in enterprise customer-support agent deals, forcing most vendors including Decagon to offer it as an option.
predictions.rationale: Salesforce and Sierra, the two most visible competitors, both moved to outcomes-based pricing within the same month, indicating convergent buyer pressure.

predictions.claim: Salesforce will publish a wave of customer case studies and adoption metrics specifically to counter the KeyBanc/analyst narrative that Agentforce lacks traction.
predictions.rationale: Repeated downgrades and public skepticism (KeyBanc, Investor's Business Daily, Yahoo Finance) create direct pressure on Salesforce to manufacture proof points.

predictions.claim: At least one more $1B+ acquisition will occur in the AI customer-support/agent space, likely a frontier lab or CRM platform acquiring a specialist voice or long-horizon agent startup.
predictions.rationale: The Intercom/Fin ($3B) and Sierra/TakeOff acquisitions in the same month suggest an active consolidation cycle rather than isolated events.

predictions.claim: Multi-model routing (dynamically switching between frontier and open-source/Chinese models based on task and cost) becomes a standard architectural feature enterprise buyers expect from agent platforms, reducing the importance of any single model partnership.
predictions.rationale: The rapid cadence of DeepSeek/Kimi/GLM releases matching frontier capability at a fraction of cost makes single-model dependency a competitive liability.

predictions.claim: Voice will overtake text/chat as the primary growth and differentiation battleground in enterprise support agents, with more telco/BPO-style exclusive distribution deals following the Sierra-SoftBank model.
predictions.rationale: ElevenLabs' valuation doubling, IBM and TELUS partnerships, and Sierra's Japan resolution-rate jump all point to voice as where budget and measurable ROI are concentrating fastest.
